who: Walter Gourlay, history faculty member at Michigan State University in the early 1970s.

evidence.says: The May 20, 1971 MSU News-Bulletin names Walter Gourlay as assistant professor of history.
The authority expands W. R. Gourlay to William Robert Gourlay and cites his A contribution towards a history of the police in Bengal (1916), identifying the author as I.C.S.

notes: The candidate is William Robert Gourlay, an earlier civil-service author, not Walter Gourlay of Michigan State.

who: William Roger Graham, historian of Canadian politics, University of Saskatchewan until 1968 and subsequently Queen’s University; PhD Toronto.

evidence.says: Identifies William Roger Graham as a historian with a Toronto PhD; he taught at Saskatchewan in Saskatoon from 1958 and moved to Queen’s in 1968; his principal work was the three-volume biography of Arthur Meighen.
William R. Graham is William Robert Graham, a physicist with a Stanford electrical-engineering PhD (1963), associated with NASA and the Office of Science and Technology Policy.
This William Graham is identified through Art and ideas: an approach to art appreciation (1971).
This William Graham authored English political philosophy from Hobbes to Maine (1899) and was a professor at Queen’s University, Belfast.

notes: Checked the supplied 40 LC records. They identify different given names or authors in other periods and fields; none identifies William Roger Graham, the Saskatchewan historian and Meighen biographer.

who: Kori A. Graves, historian of adoption and women’s history at the University at Albany; PhD history, Wisconsin-Madison, 2011.

evidence.says: Kori A. Graves’s CV lists a Wisconsin-Madison history PhD in August 2011, Albany appointments beginning in 2012, and A War Born Family among her publications.
Lists Sarah Patterson’s Being Careful dissertation among fall 2020 graduates, with Kori Graves as chair.
The authority identifies Kori A. Graves from the title page of A war born family (2019).

notes: Institution, doctorate and student match; the shared book identifies the LC candidate. The Kathleen Eleanor Cowle Graves candidate is a different person.

who: Max L. Grivno, historian of slavery and labor at the University of Southern Mississippi; PhD Maryland, 2007.

evidence.says: Max Grivno joined Southern Mississippi’s history faculty in 2007 after completing his doctorate at Maryland; his work concerns slavery, labor and the Old South.
Identifies Max L. Grivno, University of Maryland at College Park, from Historic resource study: Ferry Hill Plantation (2007).
Hayden Noel McDaniel’s fall 2019 PhD dissertation names Max Grivno as committee chair.

notes: LC affiliation and date agree with the doctorate-to-Southern-Mississippi career; the repository directly confirms the supplied student relationship.

who: Holly Grout, historian of modern France and women and gender at the University of Alabama; PhD Wisconsin (faculty page: 2008).

evidence.says: Lists Holly Grout as Alabama history faculty, with a Wisconsin PhD (2008), research in modern France and women and gender, and The Force of Beauty (2015).
Identifies Holly Grout from the title page of The force of beauty (2015).
A September 28, 2015 department news item records a celebration of faculty member Holly Grout’s The Force of Beauty.

notes: The shared book and Alabama faculty affiliation establish identity. The faculty page gives 2008 for the PhD, whereas the supplied AHA record gives 2009; this discrepancy is retained.

who: Joshua B. Guild, historian of modern African American and urban history at Princeton; PhD history and African American studies, Yale.

evidence.says: Identifies Joshua B. Guild as Princeton faculty specializing in modern African American social and cultural history and urban history, with a Yale PhD in history and African American studies.
The Joshua Guild authority cites the transcript of Oral history interview with Kalamu ya Salaam, June 5, 2006.

The introduction to Another Kind of City identifies Joshua Guild as a Princeton historian and states that he interviewed Salaam in 2006 for the Southern Oral History Program’s Imagining New Orleans project.

notes: The published interview history links the LC interviewer to the Princeton historian. Joseph Henry Guild is a different candidate.

who: Zevi Moses Gutfreund, historian of education and immigration at Louisiana State University; PhD UCLA, 2013.

The authority identifies Zevi Gutfreund (Zevi Moses), citing Speaking American (2019) and Language education, race, and the remaking of American citizenship in Los Angeles, 1900-1968.
Lists Zevi Moses Gutfreund among 2012–2013 PhD recipients with the same Language Education dissertation title.

notes: Full name, dissertation, PhD date, published book and LSU affiliation agree.

who: Phillip N. Haberkern, historian of late medieval and early modern Europe at Boston University; PhD Virginia, 2009.

Virginia’s repository identifies Phillip Nelson Haberkern’s PhD dissertation, The Presence of the Past: History, Memory, and the Making of St. Jan Hus, issued May 2009.
BU identifies Jason Macleod as studying medieval European history under Professor Phillip Haberkern.
